        pressure, a higher pressure ratio, a lower isentropic efficiency) can
        raise the heating duty a little while the COP collapses; no unit runs
        its fans that way.

        .. warning::

            The answer is only as trustworthy as the compressor correlations at
            the speeds it reaches. Those correlations are fits, and a validation
            carried out at part load does not cover the top of the speed range.
            Check that the returned ``cop_sys [-]`` is credible before using the
            ceiling, and consider lowering ``rps_max`` to the highest speed the
            validation actually reached.

        Parameters
        ----------
        T0 : float
            Outdoor air temperature [°C].
        T_a_room : float | None
            Room air temperature [°C]. Uses the constructor default if None.
        mode : str
            ``"heating"`` or ``"cooling"``.
        grid_points : int | None
            Unused. The ceiling was once swept on a grid of approach
            temperatures of this resolution; it is solved now. Accepted so
            that existing calls keep running.
        rel_tol : float
            Relative width at which the bisection on the duty stops when the
            unit cannot run flat out. A flat-out ceiling and one set by the
            indoor coil are exact.
        RH_out : float | None
            Outdoor relative humidity as a fraction (0-1) for the frost
            correction in heating. None: the frost model's default.
        RH_room : float | None
            Room relative humidity as a fraction (0-1), for the wet indoor
            coil in cooling (see :meth:`analyze_steady`). None: the dry coil.
            Not read in heating, whatever is given.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            ``Q_max [W]`` (0.0 when the unit cannot run at all here), the
            approach temperatures there, the electrical input and system COP at
            that point, and ``binding`` naming what stopped it:
            ``"compressor"`` (the speed range), ``"pressure_ratio"``,
            ``"discharge_temperature"`` or ``"condensing_temperature"`` (the
            compressor envelope: the next larger duty exceeds ``PR_cycle_max``,
            ``T_dis_max`` under its control, or ``T_cond_max``),
            ``"cycle"`` (a coil at its largest airflow and the widest
            approach the search admits), ``"cycle_invalid"`` (the next larger
            duty has no cycle the model can represent -- a condensing
            temperature at the critical point; :meth:`analyze_steady` does not
            settle on that edge) and ``"infeasible"`` when no duty has an
            operating point.

            In heating with a frosting outdoor coil the ceiling, the input and
            the COP are the mean over frosting and defrost -- what
            :meth:`analyze_steady` delivers there -- and
            ``Q_max_frost_free [W]`` is the frost-free ceiling they come from
            (``defrost_fraction [-]`` > 0). Otherwise the two are equal.

            ``Q_max [W]`` is the refrigerant-side coil heat, as
            ``Q_ref_iu [W]`` is: with ``RH_room`` in cooling it is sensible
            plus latent, and ``SHR_iu [-]`` is the sensible share of it there
            (1 for a dry coil and in heating, NaN when the unit cannot run).

            ``Q_room_sensible_at_Q_max [W]`` is the room's net sensible heat
            at that ceiling: ``Q_room_sensible [W]`` of the state the unit
            runs at there -- the coil's sensible heat less the indoor fan's
            heat in cooling, plus it in heating, under frost the mean over
            frosting and defrost -- and 0.0 when the unit cannot run. It is
            what a request made with ``request_basis="sensible"``
            gets when the search arrives at the ceiling
            (:meth:`analyze_steady`). It is the net sensible heat at the
            largest coil duty, not a maximum over the coil duties: the two
            are the same wherever the net sensible heat rises with the coil
            duty up to the ceiling, which it did at every one of 444
            conditions of default units of 2.5 to 10 kW (dry and wet
            cooling, heating). A unit with a fan held at one flow can take
            more sensible heat at a smaller coil duty (4 kW unit, outdoor
            fan held, 15 degC outdoor, saturated 35 degC room: 2,705 W at
            the 13.7 kW ceiling, 2,773 W at 13.0 kW; one of 312 conditions
            of six fan-constrained units), so it is not to be read as the
            largest sensible load such a unit can meet.

        Notes
        -----
        With ``RH_room`` in cooling the ceiling is searched together with the
        other two searches of the condition, and each takes the others'
        verified operating points for candidates: where the search on the
        duty finds none, the duty the low-load search ends on (the one
        :meth:`analyze_steady` cycles a small request at) runs, and the
        ceiling is searched upwards from it; and a flat-out ceiling of a
        unit with a fan held at one flow, on the pressure-ratio floor, is
        what the ordinary search delivers there. The answer is the same
        whatever was solved before. A request for the ``Q_max [W]``
        returned, with the same ``RH_room``, is delivered that duty with
        nothing unmet (:meth:`analyze_steady`): by the search of the
        request where it arrives there, else at this state
        (``capacity_clamped == "max"``).

        A fan held at one flow (``dV_*_fan_a_min == dV_*_fan_a_max``) leaves
        its coil one approach temperature per duty. On the pressure-ratio
        floor, with both fans held, the duties that run in continuous
        operation can then be a window a fraction of a percent wide (4 kW
        unit, 8 degC outdoor, room 35 degC saturated: 14.31 to 14.35 kW),
        or none. The searches sample the duty -- a ladder and a
        bisection, to ``rel_tol`` here -- and can miss a window narrower
        than the spacing of their samples. The result is then
        ``Q_max [W] == 0`` with ``binding == "infeasible"`` (and
        :meth:`analyze_steady` answers a request with the unit off,
        ``failure_reason == "hx_not_converged"``) although a duty inside the
        window would run. Give the fan a flow range, or request a duty
        inside the window.
        """
        if mode not in ("heating", "cooling"):
            raise ValueError(f"mode must be 'heating' or 'cooling', got {mode!r}")
        if not (math.isfinite(rel_tol) and rel_tol > 0.0):
            raise ValueError(f"rel_tol must be a positive number, got {rel_tol!r}")
        if T_a_room is None:
            T_a_room = self.T_a_room
        # Read, and checked, for the cooling ceiling only.
        RH_room = _check_room_humidity(RH_room) if RH_room is not None and mode == "cooling" else None
        with self._solving_with_room_humidity(RH_room, T_a_room, cooling=mode == "cooling"):
            return self._solve_max_capacity(T0, T_a_room, mode, rel_tol, RH_out)



    def _solve_max_capacity(
        self,
        T0: float,
        T_a_room: float,
        mode: str,
        rel_tol: float,
        RH_out: float | None,
        *,
        flat_out_only: bool = False,
    ) -> dict:
        """:meth:`max_capacity` for checked arguments, with the room humidity of the point already set.

        ``flat_out_only`` answers with the flat-out ceiling or with none
        (``binding == "infeasible"``): the search on the duty that follows
        where the unit cannot run flat out is left out.
        """
        empty = {
            "Q_max [W]": 0.0,
            "dT_ref_evap [K]": float("nan"),
            "dT_ref_cond [K]": float("nan"),
            "E_tot [W]": float("nan"),
            "cop_sys [-]": float("nan"),
            "binding": "infeasible",
            "mode": mode,
            "T0 [°C]": T0,
            "T_a_room [°C]": T_a_room,
            "Q_max_frost_free [W]": 0.0,
            "defrost_fraction [-]": 0.0,
            "SHR_iu [-]": float("nan"),
            "Q_room_sensible_at_Q_max [W]": 0.0,
        }

        sign = 1.0 if mode == "cooling" else -1.0
        wet = self._coil_may_be_wet and sign > 0
        # The ceiling of a wet condition is searched once while a solve or a
        # run is in progress: it is the same for every request of it.
        # (Not the flat-out answer alone, which is one solve and not the ceiling where it is none.)
        memo = self._wet_points if wet and not flat_out_only else None
        key = self._wet_point_key("ceiling", T0, T_a_room, float(rel_tol))
        if memo is not None and key in memo:
            return dict(memo[key])
        ceiling = self._search_max_capacity(T0, T_a_room, mode, rel_tol, RH_out, empty, flat_out_only)
        if memo is not None:
            memo[key] = dict(ceiling)
        return ceiling

    def _search_max_capacity(
        self,
        T0: float,
        T_a_room: float,
        mode: str,
        rel_tol: float,
        RH_out: float | None,
        empty: dict,
        flat_out_only: bool = False,
    ) -> dict:
        """The search of :meth:`_solve_max_capacity`; ``empty`` is its answer where no duty runs."""
        sign = 1.0 if mode == "cooling" else -1.0
        binding = "compressor"
        lo_x, lo_perf, _ = self._largest_airflow_point(sign * self._FLAT_OUT_FACTOR * self.hp_capacity, T0, T_a_room)
        if lo_x is not None and lo_perf is not None and self._coil_may_be_wet and sign > 0:
            # Flat out with a wet coil: on the pressure-ratio floor a fan held
            # at one flow delivers more than at the least-lift point.
            lo_x, lo_perf = self._flat_out_point_on_the_floor(lo_x, lo_perf, T0, T_a_room)
        if (lo_x is None or lo_perf is None) and flat_out_only:
            return empty
        if lo_x is None or lo_perf is None:
            # Not flat out: no request above the indoor coil's own limit has an
            # operating point, so the ceiling is that limit (known exactly) or
            # the largest duty below it the envelope admits.
            lo_x, lo_perf, reason = self._largest_deliverable_duty(
                sign, self._indoor_coil_limit(T_a_room), T0, T_a_room, rel_tol
            )
            # The limit itself runs: the indoor coil at its largest airflow
            # and the widest approach is what stops the unit.
            binding = BINDING_CYCLE if reason is None else self._binding_of(reason)
        if lo_x is None or lo_perf is None:
            return empty
        lo_q = abs(float(lo_perf["Q_ref_iu [W]"]))

        ceiling = {
            "Q_max [W]": lo_q,
            "dT_ref_evap [K]": lo_x[0],
            "dT_ref_cond [K]": lo_x[1],
            "E_tot [W]": float(lo_perf.get("E_tot [W]", float("nan"))),
            "cop_sys [-]": float(lo_perf.get("cop_sys [-]", float("nan"))),
            "binding": binding,
            "mode": mode,
            "T0 [°C]": T0,
            "T_a_room [°C]": T_a_room,
            "Q_max_frost_free [W]": lo_q,
            "defrost_fraction [-]": 0.0,
            "SHR_iu [-]": float(lo_perf.get("SHR_iu [-]", float("nan"))),
            # The same ceiling as the room's net sensible heat: the coil's
            # sensible heat there with the indoor fan's heat counted.
            "Q_room_sensible_at_Q_max [W]": float(lo_perf.get("Q_room_sensible [W]", float("nan"))),
        }
        frost = self._frost_state(sign, T0, RH_out, full_load=True)
        if frost.active:
            # The ceiling analyze_steady delivers: the mean over frosting and defrost.
            mean = dict(lo_perf)
            ceiling["Q_max [W]"] = self._average_over_frost(mean, frost, T0)
            ceiling["E_tot [W]"] = float(mean["E_tot [W]"])
            ceiling["cop_sys [-]"] = float(mean["cop_sys [-]"])
            ceiling["defrost_fraction [-]"] = frost.defrost_fraction
            ceiling["Q_room_sensible_at_Q_max [W]"] = float(mean["Q_room_sensible [W]"])
        return ceiling

    def _least_power_at_ceiling(self, result: dict, Q_r_iu: float, T0: float, T_a_room: float) -> dict:
        """Least-power operating point at the ceiling duty, when a coil sets the ceiling.

        The ceiling comes from the least-lift point, where both fans run at
        their largest airflow. Where a coil sets the ceiling the compressor is
        clear of its own limits and the other fan has a range to choose from:
        the indoor coil at its largest airflow and widest approach fixes the
        duty, while the outdoor fan can still trade its own power against the
        compressor's (default 4 kW unit at 7 degC: 1.3 % of the input). The
        ceiling duty is therefore solved the ordinary way, so that the row is
        the one a request arriving at the ceiling from below ends at. At the
        speed ceiling or on an envelope limit the least-lift point is the only
        one that delivers the duty, and this is not called.
        """
        delivered = abs(float(result.get("Q_ref_iu [W]", 0.0)))
        power = float(result.get("E_tot [W]", math.nan))
        if not (delivered > 0.0 and math.isfinite(power) and power > 0.0):
            return result
        duty = math.copysign(delivered, Q_r_iu)
        with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
            opt = self._optimize_operation(Q_r_iu=duty, T0=T0, T_a_room=T_a_room)
            if not (bool(getattr(opt, "success", False)) and float(opt.fun) < OBJ_CAPACITY_LIMITED):
                return result
            state = self._calc_state(dT_ref_evap=opt.x[0], dT_ref_cond=opt.x[1], Q_r_iu=duty, T0=T0, T_a_room=T_a_room)
            if state is None or not state.get("converged", False) or state.get("capacity_clamped") is not None:
                return result
            heat, input_power = abs(float(state["Q_ref_iu [W]"])), float(state["E_tot [W]"])
            if abs(heat - delivered) <= 1e-9 * delivered and input_power < power:
                state.update(
                    {
                        "capacity_clamped": CAPACITY_CLAMPED_MAX,
                        "Q_request [W]": Q_r_iu,
                        "Q_max [W]": heat,
                        "capacity_binding": result.get("capacity_binding", BINDING_CYCLE),
                    }
                )
                return state
        return result

    #: ``binding`` values of :meth:`max_capacity` that name a ceiling.
    _CEILING_BINDINGS = frozenset(
        {
            "compressor",
            BINDING_CYCLE,
            BINDING_CONDENSING,
            BINDING_DISCHARGE,
            BINDING_PRESSURE_RATIO,
        }
    )

    def _capacity_limited_operating_point(
        self, Q_r_iu: float, T0: float, T_a_room: float, *, ceiling: dict | None = None
    ) -> dict | None:
        """The state a unit runs at when the request itself has no operating point.

        Above the ceiling (:meth:`max_capacity`) that is the ceiling. A
        request below the ceiling can still be refused -- the envelope is not
        monotone in the duty: at mid speed the efficiency is lower and the
        discharge hotter than flat out -- and the unit then runs at the
        largest duty below the request that has an operating point
        (:meth:`_largest_deliverable_duty`). Either way the state is
        energy-balanced, with ``capacity_clamped == "max"``, ``Q_max [W]`` and
        ``capacity_binding``. ``None`` when the request needs no such state
        or none exists.

        A cooling request solved with a room humidity is also the ceiling's
        where it is under the ceiling by no more than the ceiling is searched
        to (:attr:`_CEILING_REL_TOL`, 0.1 %) -- the request equal to it
        first of all. The caller comes here with a request the ordinary
        search did not deliver, and that search starts from the request's
        least-lift point solved to a looser tolerance than the ceiling's
        (:attr:`_LEAST_LIFT_SEED_RTOL`, with a step into the fans' flow range
        of 1e-4 of the approaches). Close under the ceiling it reads the
        request as beyond the limit that sets the ceiling, or as short of it
        flat out, although the ceiling search has verified an operating
        point there. Measured on default units of 2 to 10 kW at 180
        conditions (20 to 46 degC outdoor, room 20 to 32 degC at 30 to 80 %):
        the request equal to the ceiling was answered with the unit off at 4
        (the limit for the reason) and up to 0.012 % short at 143, and the
        sliver of requests not delivered reached from 6.5e-6 to 6.4e-5 of
        the ceiling under it (every request 1e-4 under was delivered) --
        while a request one float step above the ceiling ran at it. Such a
        request runs at the ceiling now: the state :meth:`max_capacity`
        reported, re-solved at its approaches (:meth:`_delivering_state`),
        with ``Q_ref_iu [W]`` its ``Q_max [W]`` to rounding and nothing
        unmet.
        That is more than was asked by at most the 0.1 % the ceiling is
        known to (by the width of the sliver, in those conditions). A
        request the ordinary search delivers never comes here, and the dry
        coil's requests, and heating's, are answered as they were (the
        ceiling strictly above the request, else a search below it).

        ``ceiling`` is the ceiling of the condition where the caller has
        it in hand (the result of :meth:`max_capacity`); it is solved here
        otherwise.
        """
        mode = "cooling" if Q_r_iu > 0 else "heating"
        request = abs(Q_r_iu)
        wet = self._coil_may_be_wet and Q_r_iu > 0
        if ceiling is not None:
            pass
        elif self._RH_room is None:
            ceiling = self.max_capacity(T0=T0, T_a_room=T_a_room, mode=mode)
        else:
            # The ceiling of the same room: its humidity goes with it.
            ceiling = self.max_capacity(
                T0=T0, T_a_room=T_a_room, mode=mode, rel_tol=self._CEILING_REL_TOL, RH_room=self._RH_room
            )
        # Anything else ("infeasible", a caller's own label) is not a ceiling.
        if ceiling.get("binding") not in self._CEILING_BINDINGS:
            return None
        # The frost-free ceiling: this state is a cycle state, averaged later.
        q_ceiling = float(ceiling.get("Q_max_frost_free [W]", ceiling["Q_max [W]"]))
        if not math.isfinite(q_ceiling) or not q_ceiling > 0:
            return None
        # The request is the ceiling's: above it, or -- a wet cooling request
        # -- not under it by more than the ceiling is searched to.
        at_ceiling = q_ceiling < request or (wet and request >= q_ceiling * (1.0 - self._CEILING_REL_TOL))
        if at_ceiling:
            x = (ceiling["dT_ref_evap [K]"], ceiling["dT_ref_cond [K]"])
            binding = ceiling["binding"]
        else:
            x_below, below, reason = self._largest_deliverable_duty(
                math.copysign(1.0, Q_r_iu), request, T0, T_a_room, self._REDUCTION_REL_TOL
            )
            if x_below is None or below is None or reason is None:
                return None
            x, binding = x_below, self._binding_of(reason)
            if binding not in self._CEILING_BINDINGS:
                return None
            q_ceiling = abs(float(below["Q_ref_iu [W]"]))
            if not 0 < q_ceiling < request:
                return None
        state = self._delivering_state(x, math.copysign(q_ceiling, Q_r_iu), T0, T_a_room)
        if state is None:
            return None
        state.update(
            {
                "capacity_clamped": CAPACITY_CLAMPED_MAX,
                "Q_request [W]": Q_r_iu,
                "Q_max [W]": q_ceiling,
                "capacity_binding": binding,
            }
        )
        return state

    #: Duties tried, as fractions of the nameplate and from the bottom, to find
    #: one that runs above a request the envelope refuses from below.
    _FLOOR_LADDER: tuple[float, ...] = (0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0)
    #: Factor between the duties tried above the ladder (:meth:`_floor_rungs`).
    #: A search step, not a physical constant: the bisection that follows
    #: closes on the duty to :attr:`_FLOOR_REL_TOL` whatever it is.
    _FLOOR_CLIMB = 1.5
    #: Relative width at which the bisection for the smallest continuous duty stops.
    _FLOOR_REL_TOL = 5e-3
    #: Relative width a wet cooling point's bisection goes on to where no duty
    #: ran at :attr:`_FLOOR_REL_TOL`: the width the ceiling search closes to
    #: (the default ``rel_tol`` of :meth:`max_capacity`). A search step, not a
    #: physical constant.
    _FLOOR_FINE_REL_TOL = 1e-3
    #: Refusals a larger duty leaves behind: the limit the compressor meets
    #: towards low speed at a large lift, where the isentropic efficiency
    #: falls (:func:`~tmhp.compressor_envelope.raise_duty_within_envelope`
    #: is the boilers' counterpart).
    _REFUSED_FROM_BELOW = frozenset({DISCHARGE_TEMP_ABOVE_MAX})
    #: The same for the search of the smallest continuous duty, which also
    #: climbs past a wet cooling point's duties the fans' smallest airflows
    #: refuse (:attr:`_MIN_AIRFLOW`; never the reason of a dry solve).
    _CLIMBED_PAST = _REFUSED_FROM_BELOW | {_MIN_AIRFLOW}

    def _smallest_continuous_operating_point(self, Q_r_iu: float, T0: float, T_a_room: float) -> dict | None:
        """The smallest duty above a request the envelope refuses from below, as a continuous state.

        The compressor's speed floor is not the only lower end of continuous
        operation. At a large lift (a low-pressure refrigerant in severe cold)
        the isentropic efficiency falls towards low speed, and before
        ``rps_min`` is reached the envelope refuses the point for the
        discharge temperature, which the falling efficiency drives above
        ``T_dis_max`` even with the discharge-temperature control used up.
        Every duty below the one at which that limit lets go is refused --
        while larger duties run. A unit does not stay off there: it runs at the smallest
        duty the envelope admits and switches off when the room has had
        enough, exactly as it does below its minimum speed.

        A ladder of duties above the request is climbed past the rungs
        refused the same way to the first that is not, and a bisection closes
        on the smallest duty that runs (to :attr:`_FLOOR_REL_TOL`). The rung
        that ends the climb may itself be refused by a limit of the other
        side (the pressure ratio, a coil): the duties that run, if any, then
        lie between it and the rung below, and the bisection goes by which
        side refuses the trial. Every trial is the ordinary search
        (:meth:`_optimize_operation`), so a request at or above the duty
        returned is one :meth:`analyze_steady` solves in continuous
        operation. The state is returned with ``capacity_clamped == "min"``:
        it delivers more than the request and is averaged over the cycling
        period like a minimum-speed row (:meth:`_report_part_load`). ``None``
        when no duty runs: the limits of the two sides meet.

        A cooling point solved with a room humidity has a second lower end
        (:attr:`_MIN_AIRFLOW`): in mild weather the pressure ratio is on its
        floor, which holds the condensing temperature well above the outdoor
        air, and the evaporating temperature that would make room for the
        outdoor coil's smallest airflow makes the wet indoor coil carry more
        than a small duty at its own. Default 4 kW unit, outdoor 10 degC, room 27
        degC at 80 %: no duty below 1.54 kW runs continuously (the dry coil
        runs 1.2 kW at the same pressure ratio, 1.5). The climb passes those
        duties the same way and the unit cycles at the smallest that runs.
        With high smallest airflows that duty lies above the ladder's top,
        and the wet climb goes on to the indoor coil's limit
        (:meth:`_floor_rungs`).

        The climb (:meth:`_climb_to_continuous_duty`) starts from the
        request, so two requests of one condition can close on duties that
        differ within :attr:`_FLOOR_REL_TOL`. The dry model, as before,
        searches a condition once inside a frost balance or a dynamic run
        and reuses the state for the smaller requests that follow
        (:meth:`_remembering_floors`): such a row can differ by that
        tolerance from the same request solved alone. A wet cooling point is
        always answered as if it were solved alone -- its trials are
        remembered one by one instead (:attr:`_wet_points`), which changes
        no result. Where its own climb finds nothing at
        :attr:`_FLOOR_REL_TOL` it is bisected on to a finer width
        (:meth:`_climb_to_continuous_duty`), and where that finds nothing
        either the caller takes the flat-out state the ceiling search has
        verified (:meth:`_point_of_another_search`).
        """
        sign, request = math.copysign(1.0, Q_r_iu), abs(float(Q_r_iu))
        wet = self._coil_may_be_wet and sign > 0
        # The floor belongs to the condition, not to the request: inside one
        # frost balance or one dynamic run (the model does not change there)
        # it is searched once per condition and reused for smaller requests.
        # Not with a wet coil, whose row is that of the request solved alone
        # (see the docstring); its searches are remembered trial by trial.
        memo, key = None if wet else self._floor_memo, (sign, float(T0), float(T_a_room), self._w_room)
        if memo is not None and key in memo and request < abs(float(memo[key]["Q_ref_iu [W]"])):
            return dict(memo[key])
        found, _ = self._climb_to_continuous_duty(Q_r_iu, T0, T_a_room)
        if found is None:
            return None
        floor = dict(found[1])
        floor["capacity_clamped"] = CAPACITY_CLAMPED_MIN
        if memo is not None:
            memo[key] = dict(floor)
        return floor

    def _climb_to_continuous_duty(
        self, Q_r_iu: float, T0: float, T_a_room: float
    ) -> tuple[tuple[tuple[float, float], dict] | None, bool]:
        """The climb and the bisection of :meth:`_smallest_continuous_operating_point`, from the request.

        Returns ``(point, to_the_top)``. ``point`` is
        ``((dT_ref_evap, dT_ref_cond), state)`` of the smallest duty found
        to run in continuous operation above ``Q_r_iu``, or ``None``.
        ``to_the_top`` says the climb passed every rung, the last included,
        as refused from below: no duty tried above the request was refused
        any other way.
        The trials are the ordinary search of a duty; for a cooling
        condition solved with a room humidity each is made once while
        :attr:`_wet_points` is kept, and answered from it afterwards -- the
        approaches it ended on, from which :meth:`_calc_state` gives the
        state again.

        The bisection goes by which side refuses the trial, so it closes on
        the place where the refusal changes sides -- where the duties that
        run are, if any do. With a fan held at one flow on the
        pressure-ratio floor they can be a window narrower than
        :attr:`_FLOOR_REL_TOL` (4 kW unit with both fans held, outdoor 8
        degC, room 35 degC saturated: 14.31 to 14.35 kW, 0.23 %), which the
        bracket then closes around without a trial inside it (a 13.7 kW
        request ended between 14,304.7 and 14,371.9 W). A wet cooling point
        whose bracket closes with nothing running is therefore bisected on
        to :attr:`_FLOOR_FINE_REL_TOL`, two or three trials more. Where a
        duty ran at the first width nothing changes, and the dry search, and
        heating's, stop where they did.
        """
        sign, request = math.copysign(1.0, Q_r_iu), abs(float(Q_r_iu))
        known: dict[float, tuple[tuple[float, float] | None, str | None]] | None = None
        if self._coil_may_be_wet and sign > 0 and self._wet_points is not None:
            known = self._wet_points.setdefault(self._wet_point_key("trials", T0, T_a_room), {})

        def trial(q: float) -> tuple[dict | None, tuple[float, float] | None, str | None]:
            if known is not None and q in known:
                x, reason = known[q]
                if x is None:
                    return None, None, reason
                return (
                    self._calc_state(dT_ref_evap=x[0], dT_ref_cond=x[1], Q_r_iu=sign * q, T0=T0, T_a_room=T_a_room),
                    x,
                    None,
                )
            state, x, reason = searched(q)
            if known is not None:
                known[q] = (x, reason)
            return state, x, reason

        def searched(q: float) -> tuple[dict | None, tuple[float, float] | None, str | None]:
            opt = self._optimize_operation(Q_r_iu=sign * q, T0=T0, T_a_room=T_a_room)
            if not (bool(getattr(opt, "success", False)) and float(opt.fun) < OBJ_CAPACITY_LIMITED):
                return None, None, getattr(opt, "least_lift_reason", None)
            state = self._calc_state(
                dT_ref_evap=opt.x[0], dT_ref_cond=opt.x[1], Q_r_iu=sign * q, T0=T0, T_a_room=T_a_room
            )
            if state is None or not state.get("converged", False) or state.get("capacity_clamped") is not None:
                return None, None, None
            return state, (opt.x[0], opt.x[1]), None

        # ``q_lo`` is refused from below; ``q_hi`` runs (``running`` is its
        # state, ``x_running`` its approaches) or is refused from above.
        q_lo, q_hi, running, x_running = request, math.nan, None, None
        for q in self._floor_rungs(sign, T_a_room):
            if not q > request * (1.0 + self._FLOOR_REL_TOL):
                continue
            state, x, reason = trial(q)
            if state is None and reason in self._CLIMBED_PAST:
                q_lo = q
                continue
            q_hi, running, x_running = q, state, x
            break
        if not math.isfinite(q_hi):
            return None, True
        # A wet cooling point whose bracket closes with nothing running is
        # bisected on, to the width the ceiling search closes to (below).
        fine = self._coil_may_be_wet and sign > 0
        for rel_tol in (self._FLOOR_REL_TOL, self._FLOOR_FINE_REL_TOL):
            while q_hi - q_lo > rel_tol * q_hi:
                mid = 0.5 * (q_lo + q_hi)
                state, x, reason = trial(mid)
                if state is not None:
                    q_hi, running, x_running = mid, state, x
                elif running is not None or reason in self._CLIMBED_PAST:
                    q_lo = mid
                else:
                    q_hi = mid  # refused from above: the duties that run, if any, are below
            if running is not None or not fine:
                break
        if running is None or x_running is None:
            return None, False
        return ((float(x_running[0]), float(x_running[1])), running), False

    def _point_of_another_search(self, Q_r_iu: float, T0: float, T_a_room: float) -> dict | None:
        """The state a wet cooling request runs at where its own searches found none, from the ceiling's point.

        For a request the fans' smallest airflows refuse
        (:attr:`_MIN_AIRFLOW`) whose climb found no larger duty that runs
        (:meth:`_climb_to_continuous_duty`). The climb tries duties the
        compressor delivers inside its speed range. A unit with both fans
        held at one flow, on the pressure-ratio floor, can run at none of
        them and still run flat out -- the state the ceiling search starts
        with (:meth:`max_capacity`; 2.5 kW unit, outdoor 8 degC, room 35
        degC at 90 %: 9.61 kW). Before the request is answered with the
        unit off, that state is taken for a candidate, re-solved as a
        request of its own duty (:meth:`_delivering_state`):

        - above the request, it is the duty the request is met by cycling
          at (returned with ``capacity_clamped == "min"``, as
          :meth:`_smallest_continuous_operating_point` returns its state);
        - at the request or under it -- the least-lift point of the flat-out
          duty itself, and of a request a little above it, can read as
          refused from below -- it is where the unit runs for it, as for
          any request at or above its ceiling (``capacity_clamped ==
          "max"``, :meth:`_capacity_limited_operating_point`). The request
          equal to the flat-out duty was answered with the unit off, between
          two float neighbours that ran.

        The flat-out state is a function of the condition, so the answer is
        the same whatever was solved before. It is one solve
        (:meth:`_largest_airflow_point`), not a search: the search of the
        ceiling on the duty is not asked for here. It samples from the top
        the duties the climb has just bisected from below -- closing on the
        same place, where the refusal changes sides -- and where it ends
        with nothing it costs seconds, for a request whose own climb took a
        tenth of one. And where the climb passed every duty up to the
        indoor coil's limit as refused from below, no duty above the request
        was refused any other way: the unit is off in this weather, and
        nothing is asked.

        ``None`` when the candidate gives no state.
        """
        request = abs(float(Q_r_iu))
        # Answered from the trials the request's own climb has just made.
        _, to_the_top = self._climb_to_continuous_duty(Q_r_iu, T0, T_a_room)
        if to_the_top:
            return None
        ceiling = self._solve_max_capacity(T0, T_a_room, "cooling", self._CEILING_REL_TOL, None, flat_out_only=True)
        if ceiling.get("binding") not in self._CEILING_BINDINGS:
            return None
        q_ceiling = float(ceiling["Q_max [W]"])
        if not (math.isfinite(q_ceiling) and q_ceiling > 0.0):
            return None
        if not q_ceiling > request:
            return self._capacity_limited_operating_point(Q_r_iu, T0, T_a_room, ceiling=ceiling)
        x = (float(ceiling["dT_ref_evap [K]"]), float(ceiling["dT_ref_cond [K]"]))
        state = self._delivering_state(x, q_ceiling, T0, T_a_room)
        if state is None:
            return None
        state["capacity_clamped"] = CAPACITY_CLAMPED_MIN
        return state

    def _floor_rungs(self, sign: float, T_a_room: float) -> Iterator[float]:
        """Duties the climb for the smallest continuous duty tries, from the bottom [W].

        :attr:`_FLOOR_LADDER`, to twice the nameplate. A cooling point solved
        with a room humidity goes on from there, by :attr:`_FLOOR_CLIMB` a
        rung, to the largest duty the indoor coil carries
        (:meth:`_indoor_coil_limit`), above which no request has an operating
        point: fans with a high smallest airflow leave no continuous wet duty
        under twice the nameplate in mild weather (default 4 kW unit with
        both smallest flows at 65 % of the largest, outdoor 15 degC, room 35
        degC saturated: 8.44 kW), and the climb ends on a duty that runs or
        on one refused from above. The dry coil's climb, and heating's, ends
        where it did.
        """
        q = 0.0
        for fraction in self._FLOOR_LADDER:
            q = fraction * self.hp_capacity
            yield q
        if not (self._coil_may_be_wet and sign > 0):
            return
        top = self._indoor_coil_limit(T_a_room)
        while q < top:
            q = min(self._FLOOR_CLIMB * q, top)
            yield q

    #: Smallest continuous states found in the frost balance or dynamic run in
    #: progress, by (mode sign, T0, T_a_room, room humidity ratio); ``None`` outside one.
    _floor_memo: dict[tuple[float, float, float, float | None], dict] | None = None

    @contextlib.contextmanager
    def _remembering_floors(self) -> Iterator[None]:
        """Reuse :meth:`_smallest_continuous_operating_point` results while the block runs."""
        outer = self._floor_memo
        if outer is None:
            self._floor_memo = {}
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            self._floor_memo = outer

    # =============================================================
    # Steady-state analysis
    # =============================================================



[docs]
    @steady_notice(delivered_key="Q_ref_iu [W]")
    @steady_envelope()
    def analyze_steady(
        self,
        Q_r_iu: float,
        T0: float,
        T_a_room: float | None = None,
        *,
        return_dict: bool = True,
        postprocess: bool = True,
        verbose: bool = True,
        RH_out: float | None = None,
        RH_room: float | None = None,
        request_basis: str = REQUEST_BASIS_TOTAL,
    ) -> dict | pd.DataFrame:
        """Run a steady-state performance snapshot.

        Parameters
        ----------
        Q_r_iu : float
            Indoor thermal load [W]. >0 cooling, <0 heating, 0 off. With the
            default ``request_basis`` it is the
            heat the refrigerant exchanges with the room air at the indoor
            coil (``Q_ref_iu [W]``): in cooling the coil's total heat,
            sensible plus latent, before the indoor fan's heat. What the room
            receives is reported as ``Q_room_sensible [W]`` and
            ``Q_iu_latent [W]`` (below). With
            ``request_basis="sensible"`` it is the net sensible heat
            the room air gives up (cooling) or receives (heating).
        T0 : float
            Dead-state / outdoor-air temperature [°C].
        T_a_room : float | None
            Room air temperature [°C]. Uses constructor default if None.
        return_dict : bool
            If True return dict; else single-row DataFrame.
        postprocess : bool
            If True, apply postprocess_exergy to the output.
        verbose : bool
            If False, the :class:`~tmhp.OperatingLimitWarning` of this call
            is not issued (the row is the same).
        RH_out : float | None
            Outdoor relative humidity as a fraction (0-1), used by the frost
            correction in heating. None: the frost model's default (0.84).
        RH_room : float | None
            Room relative humidity as a fraction (0-1) at ``T_a_room`` and
            one standard atmosphere. With it, a cooling coil whose surface --
            taken at the evaporating temperature -- is below the room air's
            dew point condenses water (the wet coil of
            :func:`tmhp.heat_exchanger.calc_HX_perf_for_target_heat`), and
            the request ``Q_r_iu`` is met by sensible plus latent heat. None
            (default): the dry coil, all of the coil heat sensible. Not read
            on a heating request, where the indoor coil is the condenser, nor
            on an off one (``Q_r_iu <= 0``): anything may be given there. On
            a cooling request a value that is not a number in 0-1 raises
            ``ValueError``.
        request_basis : str
            What ``Q_r_iu`` is a request for. ``"total"`` (default): the
            refrigerant-side heat of the indoor coil, ``Q_ref_iu [W]``.
            ``"sensible"``: the net sensible heat of the room air,
            ``Q_room_sensible [W]`` -- the sensible load a zone of a building
            simulation hands over. The coil then has to carry more than the
            request in cooling (the indoor fan's heat, and with ``RH_room``
            the latent heat of the water it condenses) and less in heating
            (the fan's heat is part of what the room receives), and the
            model finds the coil duty at which ``Q_room_sensible [W]`` of the
            row equals the request (see *Notes*). Any other value raises
            ``ValueError``.

        Returns
        -------
        dict | pd.DataFrame
            Cycle state plus diagnostic flags.

            Two keys are useful for branching:

            - ``"converged"`` (bool) — True only when the inner HX optimisation
              and the SciPy optimiser both succeeded.
            - ``"failure_reason"`` (str) — one of ``"none"``, ``"cycle_invalid"``
              (the refrigerant cycle itself was infeasible), ``"pr_above_max"``,
              ``"discharge_temp_above_max"``, ``"condensing_temp_above_max"``
              (the
              compressor envelope refuses the request where it is easiest to
              meet -- at its least-lift point -- and no smaller duty runs
              either; a request that a smaller duty meets returns that duty
              with ``capacity_clamped="max"`` and ``capacity_binding`` naming
              the limit: ``"discharge_temperature"``,
              ``"condensing_temperature"`` for ``T_cond_max``),
              ``"hx_not_converged"`` (cycle OK
              but a coil cannot carry the duty inside the approach bounds), or
              ``"optimizer_failed"`` (SciPy reported ``success=False``).

            ASHP triggers an off-mode fallback for any of the non-``"none"``
            reasons — ``E_cmp [W]`` will be 0 and the COP keys will be NaN
            in that case. Treat ``failure_reason != "none"`` as "do not
            trust the numbers".

            Part load is reported on every row: ``Q_request [W]`` (signed,
            as asked), ``Q_unmet [W]`` (request not delivered, >= 0),
            ``runtime_fraction [-]``, ``capacity_ratio [-]``,
            ``part_load_factor [-]``, ``Q_min [W]`` and
            ``E_cycling_loss [W]``. A request below the minimum continuous
            capacity (``capacity_clamped == "min"``) is the mean over an
            on/off cycling period: ``Q_ref_iu [W]`` equals the request,
            heat and flow rates are the running values times
            ``capacity_ratio [-]`` (the indoor fan's power with them),
            compressor and outdoor-fan power the running values times
            ``runtime_fraction [-]``, and the COP keys carry the EN 14825
            degradation; temperatures, pressures and speed are those of
            the running machine (:mod:`tmhp.cycling`). A request above
            the ceiling (``capacity_clamped == "max"``) adds ``Q_max [W]``
            and ``capacity_binding`` (``"compressor"``,
            ``"discharge_temperature"``, ``"condensing_temperature"``,
            ``"pressure_ratio"`` or ``"cycle"``; see
            :meth:`max_capacity`).

            Heating below the frost model's outdoor limit (5 degC; the
            correction grows to its full size at 2 degC) is
            the mean over frosting and defrost (:mod:`tmhp.defrost`):
            ``defrost_fraction [-]`` is the share of the runtime spent
            defrosting, ``frost_capacity_factor [-]`` and
            ``frost_power_factor [-]`` the multipliers of the frosted coil,
            ``E_defrost [W]`` and ``Q_defrost [W]`` the mean power and room
            heat the defrost takes, and ``Q_ref_iu_frost_free [W]`` /
            ``E_tot_frost_free [W]`` the frost-free cycle the row was solved
            at. Without frost those two repeat ``Q_ref_iu [W]`` and
            ``E_tot [W]``.

            The indoor coil's heat is split on every row:
            ``Q_iu_sensible [W]`` and ``Q_iu_latent [W]`` (air side, before
            the fan; their sum is ``Q_ref_iu [W]`` within the coil solver's
            tolerance), ``SHR_iu [-]`` their sensible share,
            ``m_dot_iu_condensate [kg/s]`` the water condensed, and
            ``w_iu_a_in [kg/kg]`` / ``w_iu_a_out [kg/kg]`` the humidity ratio
            of the air entering and leaving the unit, with ``RH_room [-]``
            the room humidity used (the three NaN without one). Latent heat
            is zero for a dry coil. ``Q_room_sensible [W]`` is the net
            sensible heat the room air gives up (cooling:
            ``Q_iu_sensible - E_iu_fan``) or receives (heating:
            ``Q_iu_sensible + E_iu_fan``), the indoor fan's heat counted.

            With ``RH_room`` in cooling both ends of the range are the wet
            coil's. A request above its ceiling runs there
            (``capacity_clamped == "max"``; :meth:`max_capacity` with the
            same ``RH_room``). A request equal to the ceiling is delivered
            it, with ``Q_unmet [W]`` zero: as an ordinary row
            (``capacity_clamped`` ``None``) where the search of the request
            delivers that duty, and otherwise as the ceiling's own state
            (``capacity_clamped == "max"``, ``Q_ref_iu [W]`` the
            ``Q_max [W]`` :meth:`max_capacity` reports, to rounding). The
            ceiling's state also answers a request the search does not
            deliver that is under the ceiling by no more than the 0.1 % the
            ceiling is searched to, which is up to that 0.1 % more than was
            asked (measured on default units: 0.006 %). A request the
            search delivers is an ordinary row at any distance from the
            ceiling. In mild weather, on the pressure-ratio floor,
            the fans' smallest airflows leave no continuous operation below
            some duty; a smaller request is met by cycling at that duty
            (``capacity_clamped == "min"``, ``Q_min [W]``). Where the
            search above the request finds no such duty, the state the unit
            runs flat out at is taken -- the one the ceiling search of
            :meth:`max_capacity` starts with -- which the request is met by
            cycling at when it lies above the request and where the unit
            runs when it lies under it; and where no duty is
            found to run the row is off with
            ``failure_reason == "hx_not_converged"`` (a fan held at one flow
            can leave a window of duties too narrow for the searches to hit:
            see the notes of :meth:`max_capacity`). Without ``RH_room``
            such a request is answered as before, with the unit off and
            ``"cycle_invalid"``. On a row whose coil removes water
            (``Q_iu_latent [W]`` > 0) the exergy columns ``Xc_iu_hx [W]``,
            ``X_eff_iu_hx [-]`` and ``X_eff_sys [-]`` are NaN
            (:meth:`postprocess_exergy`).

            ``Q_request [W]`` and ``Q_unmet [W]`` are on the basis of
            ``Q_r_iu``, which ``request_basis`` names on every row. With
            ``"total"``: refrigerant-side coil heat, total (sensible plus
            latent) and before the fan heat -- not the room-side
            ``Q_room_sensible [W]``. With ``"sensible"``: that
            room-side heat, ``Q_unmet [W]`` being what
            ``Q_room_sensible [W]`` is short of the request. Every other key
            means the same on either basis: ``Q_ref_iu [W]``, ``Q_max [W]``
            and ``Q_min [W]`` are coil heat. ``cop_sys [-]`` is on the room
            side: ``Q_room_sensible [W]`` plus ``Q_iu_latent [W]`` over
            ``E_tot [W]``.

            A row asked with ``"sensible"`` has one key more, after the
            others: ``request_solves [-]`` (int), the number of total-basis
            solves the search of the request took -- what the row cost, in
            solves of ``request_basis="total"``. It is 0 for a zero request,
            which is not searched, and never above
            :attr:`_ROOM_SENSIBLE_MAX_SOLVES`; a row short of its request
            that took them all is one the search did not finish (*Notes*). A
            total-basis row does not have the key.

        Warns
        -----
        OperatingLimitWarning
            Once, when the compressor was asked to run and the result is the
            off state (``failure_reason`` other than ``"none"``) or a running
            point that delivers less than the request (``capacity_clamped ==
            "max"``): the request, what is delivered, the limit in words and
            what removes it. Issued once per model and limit unless the
            ``"always"`` filter is set (:mod:`tmhp.operating_limits`).

        Notes
        -----
        A request on the room's net sensible heat
        (``request_basis="sensible"``) is answered with the row of a
        coil duty -- the row ``request_basis="total"`` returns for that duty,
        key for key, with ``Q_request [W]``, ``Q_unmet [W]`` and
        ``request_basis`` written over, and ``request_solves [-]`` added.
        The duty is searched: the request itself first, then that duty
        scaled by the request over the net sensible heat it gave, then by
        the secant through the last two duties; a search that five solves
        have not ended, with trials on both sides of the request, takes its
        steps from the trials of each side, which is what closes on a duty
        just beyond a kink of the net sensible heat
        (:meth:`_solve_room_sensible`). ``Q_room_sensible [W]`` is read
        from the row as it is
        reported, so a request the unit meets by cycling, and a heating
        request with frost on the outdoor coil, are matched in their means.
        While the compressor is off the indoor fan is off with it: a cycling
        row carries the running coil heat, the fan's power and so the net
        sensible heat all times ``capacity_ratio [-]`` (:mod:`tmhp.cycling`),
        and nothing for a fan that circulates air between the compressor's
        runs.

        The match is to 1e-6 of the request where the first three solves
        reach it, which they do on a row whose coil is dry (no ``RH_room``,
        a coil above the room's dew point, heating) of a unit whose fans
        modulate: such a row is smooth along the duty. Otherwise it is to
        1e-4. On a row that condenses water the operating point of a duty is
        the optimiser's, located to 1e-3 K of approach and 0.1 W of input,
        and the sensible share of neighbouring wet duties scatters by up to
        that much; a fan held at one flow scatters a dry row by about 1e-5
        (:attr:`_ROOM_SENSIBLE_LOOSE_RTOL`). A row inside the tolerance is
        met, ``Q_unmet [W]`` zero. The ``Q_ref_iu [W]`` the row reports is
        the coil duty that was solved, to rounding: asked again for it as
        ``request_basis="total"``, a unit whose fans modulate repeats the row
        (every numeric key to 1e-12 on 2,646 requests of default units, wet
        rows included). A unit with a fan held at one flow repeats it to the
        scatter of its own rows: its search can end on either of two
        operating points for duties one rounding apart (4 kW unit with the
        indoor fan held, 25/35 degC, 4,023.127 W: 568.58 W of input with
        60.9 W at the outdoor fan, or 568.14 W with 54.6 W).

        The search ends without a match on

        - a row at a limit: the coil duty asked for is delivered short
          (``capacity_clamped == "max"``) with less net sensible heat than
          the request. Above the ceiling of the condition that is the
          ceiling's row, the largest coil duty the unit delivers
          (:meth:`max_capacity`, ``Q_room_sensible_at_Q_max [W]``); the rest is
          ``Q_unmet [W]``. Where an earlier trial delivered more net
          sensible heat (an indoor fan whose heat grows faster than the
          coil's sensible heat), that trial is the answer;
        - an off row (``failure_reason`` other than ``"none"``): the model
          answers the coil duty tried with the unit off. A unit with a fan
          held at one flow can have such duties below its ceiling, and
          duties delivered short (see :meth:`max_capacity`); the duties
          around the first one tried are not searched. The answer is the
          trial that comes closest to the request from below, the off row
          (nothing delivered) among them. Where the off row is the first
          trial it is the answer, with the whole request unmet; after a
          trial that delivered some net sensible heat, that trial is;
        - a row that delivers more than the request where no duty tried
          delivers less (a unit without the cycling model, below its
          smallest continuous duty), with nothing unmet, as on the coil
          basis;
        - after :attr:`_ROOM_SENSIBLE_MAX_SOLVES` solves, the row that comes
          closest to the request from below, with what is missing in
          ``Q_unmet [W]``. A unit with its outdoor fan held at one flow can
          pass from one indoor airflow to another between two neighbouring
          coil duties, and its net sensible heat with it (4 kW unit, 35 degC
          outdoor, room 35 degC at 60 %: 1,665 W at a coil duty of 3,571 W,
          2,490 W at 3,586 W); a request between the two is answered with
          the lower row.
        """
        validate_steady(locals())
        request_basis = _check_request_basis(request_basis)

        if T_a_room is None:
            T_a_room = self.T_a_room
        # Read, and checked, on a cooling request only: a heating or an off
        # point has no use for it, whatever it is given.
        RH_room = _check_room_humidity(RH_room) if RH_room is not None and Q_r_iu > 0 else None

        solves = 0
        if request_basis == REQUEST_BASIS_SENSIBLE and Q_r_iu != 0:
            # The coil duty whose row has the requested net sensible heat.
            result, solves = self._solve_room_sensible(
                Q_r_iu, T0, T_a_room, postprocess=postprocess, verbose=verbose, RH_out=RH_out, RH_room=RH_room
            )
        else:
            # A cooling point with a room humidity is solved with the wet indoor
            # coil; any other point with the dry one.
            with self._solving_with_room_humidity(RH_room, T_a_room, cooling=Q_r_iu > 0):
                result = self._solve_steady(
                    Q_r_iu, T0, T_a_room, postprocess=postprocess, verbose=verbose, RH_out=RH_out
                )
        if result:
            result[REQUEST_BASIS_KEY] = request_basis
            if request_basis == REQUEST_BASIS_SENSIBLE:
                # What the row cost: the last key, on rows of this basis only.
                result[REQUEST_SOLVES_KEY] = solves

        if return_dict:
            return result
        return pd.DataFrame([result]) if result else pd.DataFrame()



    #: Relative tolerance to which ``Q_room_sensible [W]`` is matched with a
    #: request on that basis (``request_basis="sensible"``) by the first
    #: :attr:`_ROOM_SENSIBLE_STRICT_SOLVES` solves of a row whose coil is dry.
    #: A search tolerance, not a physical constant: such a row of a unit
    #: whose fans modulate is smooth along the coil duty (its net sensible
    #: heat departs from a straight line by less than 6e-7 of itself over
    #: 1 % of the duty, default 4 kW unit at 35/27 degC), and the secant
    #: reaches 1e-6 on its third solve.
    _ROOM_SENSIBLE_RTOL = 1e-6
    #: The tolerance of a row that condenses water (``Q_iu_latent [W]`` > 0),
    #: and of any row from the solve after
    #: :attr:`_ROOM_SENSIBLE_STRICT_SOLVES` on. The operating point of a duty
    #: is where the refinement of :meth:`_optimize_operation` stops -- 1e-3 K
    #: of approach, 0.1 W of input -- and a wet coil's sensible share moves
    #: with the evaporating approach, so the net sensible heat of
    #: neighbouring wet duties scatters around a smooth curve: by up to
    #: 1.1e-4 of itself in the scans it was measured on (default 4 kW unit,
    #: 35/27 degC at 50 %, 4.97 kW: 0.39 W of 3,599 W over 81 duties 0.005 %
    #: apart; 30/27 degC at 80 %, 3 kW: 4e-5). A dry row of a unit with a fan
    #: held at one flow scatters too, by about 1e-5 (both fans of a 4 kW unit
    #: held, 46/27 degC, 2 kW: a step of 0.018 W between duties 0.0003 W
    #: apart). No duty need have a net sensible heat closer to the request
    #: than that scatter, so a search that has not arrived by then is not
    #: held to 1e-6.
    _ROOM_SENSIBLE_LOOSE_RTOL = 1e-4
    #: Solves a dry row is held to :attr:`_ROOM_SENSIBLE_RTOL` for: the
    #: request, the first guess from it, and one secant step, which is where
    #: a smooth row arrives.
    _ROOM_SENSIBLE_STRICT_SOLVES = 3
    #: Factor by which the outer search moves the coil duty where every trial
    #: so far lies on one side of the request and the secant through the last
    #: two points the wrong way, or nowhere: the net sensible heat is not
    #: monotone in the coil duty everywhere (a wet coil that cycles on the
    #: pressure-ratio floor: default 2.5 kW unit, 20 degC outdoor, room 30
    #: degC at 50 %, 119.8 W at a coil duty of 135.5 W and 118.3 W at
    #: 158.2 W). A search step, not a physical constant: the trials that
    #: follow close on the duty whatever it is.
    _ROOM_SENSIBLE_GROWTH = 1.5
    #: Solves up to which a search with trials on both sides of the request
    #: takes the secant through its last two trials; from the next one on it
    #: takes its step from the trials of each side
    #: (:meth:`_solve_room_sensible`). A step of the search, not a physical
    #: constant. Where the net sensible heat is smooth along the coil duty
    #: that secant is the quickest of the steps tried and arrives within five
    #: solves: 1,936 of the 1,950 requests met on the grid of
    #: :attr:`_ROOM_SENSIBLE_MAX_SOLVES`, and 1,482 of 1,490 on six units
    #: with a fan held at one flow; steps from the sides from the first
    #: bracket on took 3.45 solves a request on that grid instead of 2.91.
    #: A search
    #: still open then is at a kink or a step of the net sensible heat, where
    #: the last two trials lie on either side of it and their secant closes
    #: on the request only linearly. The default 2.5 kW unit at 20 degC
    #: outdoor with the room at 29.9 degC and 50 % cycles with a running
    #: state that changes with the request below a coil duty of 205.2 W and
    #: does not above it: 0.22 W of net sensible heat per W of coil heat
    #: below, 0.61 W above. The request for 125.25 W, whose duty is 0.2 W
    #: above the kink, was 0.05 W short after twelve such secants and is met
    #: in eight solves by the steps from the sides.
    _ROOM_SENSIBLE_SECANT_SOLVES = 5
    #: Total-basis solves one request on the room's net sensible heat may
    #: take. A budget of the search, not a physical constant: on 2,646
    #: requests of three default units (2.5 to 10 kW, dry and wet, cooling
    #: and heating) a request that was met took 2.8 solves on a dry row and
    #: 4.1 on a wet one on average, at most four on a dry row and at most
    #: seven on 846 of the 848 wet ones; the other two took eight (one of
    #: them the cycling unit of :attr:`_ROOM_SENSIBLE_GROWTH`, where the
    #: search first has to pass a stretch along which the net sensible heat
    #: falls). Among 528 requests around the kink of
    #: :attr:`_ROOM_SENSIBLE_SECANT_SOLVES` the most was ten. A search
    #: that uses the budget up without a match has tried no duty with the
    #: requested net sensible heat (:meth:`_solve_room_sensible`).
    _ROOM_SENSIBLE_MAX_SOLVES = 12

    def _solve_room_sensible(
        self,
        Q_r_iu: float,
        T0: float,
        T_a_room: float,
        *,
        postprocess: bool,
        verbose: bool,
        RH_out: float | None,
        RH_room: float | None,
    ) -> tuple[dict, int]:
        """:meth:`analyze_steady` for a request on the room's net sensible heat (checked arguments, not zero).

        Returns the row and the number of total-basis solves it took
        (``request_solves [-]``). The row is the row of a coil duty, solved
        the ordinary way
        (``request_basis="total"``), in which ``Q_request [W]`` and
        ``Q_unmet [W]`` are then written on the basis of the request. The
        duty is found by an outer search on it, every trial a total-basis
        solve whose ``Q_room_sensible [W]`` is read as the row reports it
        (the mean over a cycling period, and over frosting and defrost):

        1. the request itself. In cooling it gives too little (the coil's
           heat less the latent part and the fan's heat), in heating too
           much (the coil's heat plus the fan's);
        2. that duty times the request over the net sensible heat it gave
           -- exact for a cycling row, whose heats all scale with the
           capacity ratio, and the fan heat (dry coil) or the sensible heat
           ratio (wet coil) of the first solve otherwise. Where the first
           solve gives zero or negative net sensible heat -- in cooling, an
           indoor fan whose heat is at least the coil's sensible heat, which
           only a fan far less efficient than the default reaches -- there
           is nothing to scale by, and twice the request is taken, the
           largest step step 3 takes upwards;
        3. the secant through the last two trials. Where trials lie on both
           sides of the request and the secant leaves the interval between
           the closest of them (the bracket), its middle is taken. Where
           every trial so far gives too little, the duty is above them all:
           the secant is kept if it points there, by no more than a factor
           two, and :attr:`_ROOM_SENSIBLE_GROWTH` times the largest duty
           tried is taken otherwise (the net sensible heat is not monotone
           in the coil duty everywhere); likewise downwards where every
           trial gives too much;
        4. from the solve after :attr:`_ROOM_SENSIBLE_SECANT_SOLVES` on, in
           a bracket: a step from the trials of each side of the request.
           The line through the two trials closest to the bracket under the
           request, and the line through the two closest over it, each
           name a duty; of those inside the bracket the one nearer to where
           the chord between the bracket's ends meets the request is taken,
           and the bracket's middle where neither is inside.

        Step 4 is for a net sensible heat with a kink or a step along the
        coil duty, which is where a search is still open by then. The net
        sensible heat is smooth in stretches: a kink is where condensation
        sets in or where the running state of a cycling unit stops changing
        with the request, a step where the operating point of a unit with a
        fan held at one flow passes from one airflow to another. Just past
        a kink the secant through the last two trials, which lie on either
        side of it, closes on the request only linearly. Two trials on the
        request's own side of the kink lie on its stretch, and the line
        through them names the duty as closely as that stretch is straight
        -- exactly on a cycling row, whose heats all scale with the capacity
        ratio. Where the net sensible heat bends one way between the trials
        the lines of both sides err to the same side of the duty and the
        chord to the other, so the line nearer the chord is the closer of
        the two. A line that leaves the bracket says the request is not
        reached along its stretch -- a step, or a kink beyond the other end
        -- and the middle halves the bracket, which is what closes on a
        step.

        The bracketing methods of the textbooks were measured beside it,
        each from the first bracket on, and not taken. For the request of
        :attr:`_ROOM_SENSIBLE_SECANT_SOLVES`, 0.2 W above a kink: false
        position with the Illinois correction twelve solves (the whole
        budget), Brent's method ten, the steps above eight; over the 528
        requests around it at most twelve, eleven and ten. Neither is as
        quick as the secant where the row is smooth: 2.918 and 2.908 solves
        a request on the grid of :attr:`_ROOM_SENSIBLE_MAX_SOLVES` against
        2.906, and 2.575 and 2.547 against 2.546 on six units with a fan
        held (the search as it is: 2.905 and 2.546). Both interpolate
        between the bracket's ends, which lie on either side of a kink
        until the bracket has closed past it.

        The search ends on a trial whose net sensible heat is within the
        tolerance of the request: :attr:`_ROOM_SENSIBLE_RTOL` for the first
        :attr:`_ROOM_SENSIBLE_STRICT_SOLVES` trials of a dry coil,
        :attr:`_ROOM_SENSIBLE_LOOSE_RTOL` where the trial's coil condenses
        water and for every later trial. It also ends on a trial that says
        no other duty is the unit's answer:

        - the unit delivers the coil duty short (``capacity_clamped ==
          "max"`` with coil heat unmet) and its net sensible heat is under
          the request: the unit is at a limit. A coil duty above the ceiling
          of the condition gives the ceiling's row, so this is where a
          request above the largest net sensible heat ends;
        - the unit is off (``failure_reason`` set): the coil duty has no
          operating point and no smaller one is run in its place. Duties
          around it are not tried.

        Two trials with the same net sensible heat are a unit without the
        cycling model below its smallest duty; what follows applies where
        the later of them did not end the search (met, off, or short of the
        request at a limit, above). Under the request the search
        goes on: inside the bracket where a trial over the request lies
        above them (its middle, or the step of step 4 from the solve named
        there on), and otherwise :attr:`_ROOM_SENSIBLE_GROWTH` times higher,
        twice where no trial has yet given positive net sensible heat, as
        every step up then is. Over the request they end it.

        Where the trials stop moving (two with the same net sensible heat
        over the request), where
        :attr:`_ROOM_SENSIBLE_MAX_SOLVES` are used up, or where the search
        ends on one of the two trials above, no duty tried has the
        requested net sensible heat. The answer is then the trial that comes
        closest to the request from below, so that what is missing shows as
        ``Q_unmet [W]``; where every trial delivers more than the request,
        the one that delivers least. This is where the total-basis rows of
        neighbouring duties are not neighbours themselves -- a unit with its
        outdoor fan held at one flow whose operating point passes from one
        indoor airflow to another between two duties (4 kW unit, 35 degC
        outdoor, room 35 degC at 60 %: 1,665 W of net sensible heat at a
        coil duty of 3,571 W, 2,490 W at 3,586 W) has no duty for a request
        between the two.

        The trials of a wet cooling condition share what its searches find
        (:meth:`_sharing_wet_points`), which changes none of them; nothing
        else is carried from one trial to the next, and nothing from one
        request to another: the row is a function of the request and the
        condition.
        """
        sign, request = math.copysign(1.0, Q_r_iu), abs(float(Q_r_iu))
        # The trials in the order solved: (coil duty the row sits at, its net
        # sensible heat, the row).
        trials: list[tuple[float, float, dict]] = []
        met = False  # whether the last trial has the requested net sensible heat

        def tolerance(row: dict) -> float:
            """Largest difference from the request at which ``row``, the last trial, is met."""
            wet = float(row.get("Q_iu_latent [W]", 0.0)) > 0.0
            strict = not wet and len(trials) <= self._ROOM_SENSIBLE_STRICT_SOLVES
            return (self._ROOM_SENSIBLE_RTOL if strict else self._ROOM_SENSIBLE_LOOSE_RTOL) * request

        def solve(duty: float) -> bool:
            """Solve the total-basis row of ``duty``; whether the search ends on it."""
            nonlocal met
            row = self.analyze_steady(
                Q_r_iu=sign * duty,
                T0=T0,
                T_a_room=T_a_room,
                return_dict=True,
                postprocess=postprocess,
                verbose=verbose,
                RH_out=RH_out,
                RH_room=RH_room,
            )
            assert isinstance(row, dict)
            running = bool(row.get("hp_is_on", False)) and row.get("failure_reason", "none") == "none"
            sensible = float(row.get("Q_room_sensible [W]", 0.0)) if running else 0.0
            if not math.isfinite(sensible):
                sensible = 0.0
            # Delivered short of the coil duty asked for: the row sits at the
            # duty it delivers, and no larger request moves it.
            short = (
                running
                and row.get("capacity_clamped") == CAPACITY_CLAMPED_MAX
                and float(row.get("Q_unmet [W]", 0.0)) > 0.0
            )
            trials.append((abs(float(row["Q_ref_iu [W]"])) if short else duty, sensible, row))
            met = running and abs(sensible - request) <= tolerance(row)
            return met or not running or (short and sensible < request)

        def step_from_the_sides(under: float, over: float) -> float:
            """A duty inside the bracket ``(under, over)``, from the trials of each side of the request (step 4)."""
            # By duty: the bracket's end last of those under the request, first of those over it.
            lower = sorted(t[:2] for t in trials if t[1] < request)[-2:]
            upper = sorted(t[:2] for t in trials if t[1] > request)[:2]
            chord = under + (request - lower[-1][1]) * (over - under) / (upper[0][1] - lower[-1][1])
            steps = []
            for side in (lower[::-1], upper):
                if len(side) < 2:
                    continue
                (near, sensible_near), (far, sensible_far) = side
                if sensible_near != sensible_far:
                    step = near + (request - sensible_near) * (near - far) / (sensible_near - sensible_far)
                    if under < step < over:
                        steps.append(step)
            return min(steps, key=lambda step: abs(step - chord)) if steps else 0.5 * (under + over)

        def next_duty() -> float | None:
            """The coil duty to try after the trials made; ``None`` where they give none."""
            duty, sensible, _ = trials[-1]
            if len(trials) == 1:
                # No net sensible heat to scale by (the fan's heat at least
                # the coil's sensible heat): the duty is above, by the
                # largest step that step 3 takes upwards.
                return request * duty / sensible if sensible > 0.0 else 2.0 * duty
            before, sensible_before, _ = trials[-2]
            if duty == before:
                return None
            # Where no trial has cooled the room yet (the fan's heat at least
            # the coil's sensible heat in every one), the slope says nothing
            # of how far the duty is: the largest step upwards.
            grow = 2.0 if max(t[1] for t in trials) <= 0.0 else self._ROOM_SENSIBLE_GROWTH
            under = max((t[0] for t in trials if t[1] < request), default=math.nan)
            over = min((t[0] for t in trials if t[1] > request), default=math.nan)
            if sensible == sensible_before:
                # Flat: a unit without the cycling model below its smallest
                # duty. Over the request that row is the answer; under it
                # (the fan's heat outweighs the coil's) the duty is above --
                # inside the bracket where a trial over the request lies
                # above, by the bracket's rule (middle, then step 4).
                if sensible > request:
                    return None
                if not under < over:
                    return grow * max(duty, before)
                if len(trials) >= self._ROOM_SENSIBLE_SECANT_SOLVES:
                    return step_from_the_sides(under, over)
                return 0.5 * (under + over)
            step = duty + (request - sensible) * (duty - before) / (sensible - sensible_before)
            if under < over:
                # Trials on both sides: the duty lies between the closest two.
                if len(trials) >= self._ROOM_SENSIBLE_SECANT_SOLVES:
                    # Not found where a smooth row is: a kink or a step.
                    step = step_from_the_sides(under, over)
                elif not under < step < over:
                    step = 0.5 * (under + over)
            elif math.isnan(over):
                # Every trial gives too little: the duty is above them all,
                # whatever the last two say of the slope.
                if grow == 2.0 or not under < step <= 2.0 * under:
                    step = grow * under
            elif math.isnan(under):
                # Every trial gives too much: below them all.
                if not 0.5 * over <= step < over:
                    step = over / grow
            else:
                # Both sides, out of order along the duty (not monotone there).
                step = min(max(step, 0.5 * duty), 2.0 * duty)
            if not (math.isfinite(step) and step > 0.0) or step == duty:
                return None
            return step

        ended = False
        duty: float | None = request
        # What the wet coil's searches find of the condition serves every trial.
        with self._sharing_wet_points():
            for _ in range(self._ROOM_SENSIBLE_MAX_SOLVES):
                assert duty is not None
                ended = solve(duty)
                if ended:
                    break
                duty = next_duty()
                if duty is None:
                    break
        if met:
            _, sensible, result = trials[-1]
        else:
            # No trial has the requested net sensible heat (or the last is
            # the unit off or at its ceiling, which an earlier trial may beat
            # where the net sensible heat falls with the duty): the closest
            # from below, else the least of those above.
            below = [t for t in trials if t[1] < request]
            _, sensible, result = max(below, key=lambda t: t[1]) if below else min(trials, key=lambda t: t[1])

        result["Q_request [W]"] = float(Q_r_iu)
        unmet = request - sensible
        result["Q_unmet [W]"] = unmet if unmet > self._ROOM_SENSIBLE_LOOSE_RTOL * request else 0.0
        # The binding of the row was settled by the solve it came from: the
        # envelope's check of this call (:func:`~tmhp.compressor_envelope.steady_envelope`)
        # has nothing left to solve again.
        self._condensing_rejected = False
        return result, len(trials)

    def _solve_steady(
        self, Q_r_iu: float, T0: float, T_a_room: float, *, postprocess: bool, verbose: bool, RH_out: float | None
    ) -> dict:
        """:meth:`analyze_steady` for checked arguments, with the room humidity of the point already set."""
        # Heating with a frosting outdoor coil is the mean over frosting and
        # defrost: solved frost-free at a larger duty, then averaged.
        frost = self._frost_state(Q_r_iu, T0, RH_out)
        if frost.active:
            # The frost balance solves the frost-free cycle at several duties.
            with self._remembering_floors():
                return self._analyze_steady_frosted(
                    frost, Q_r_iu, T0, T_a_room, postprocess=postprocess, verbose=verbose
                )

        if Q_r_iu == 0:
            result: dict | None = self._calc_state(
                dT_ref_evap=5.0,
                dT_ref_cond=5.0,
                Q_r_iu=0.0,
                T0=T0,
                T_a_room=T_a_room,
            )
            if result is not None:
                result["failure_reason"] = "none"
        else:
            opt_result = self._optimize_operation(
                Q_r_iu=Q_r_iu,
                T0=T0,
                T_a_room=T_a_room,
            )
            result = None
            with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
                result = self._calc_state(
                    dT_ref_evap=opt_result.x[0],
                    dT_ref_cond=opt_result.x[1],
                    Q_r_iu=Q_r_iu,
                    T0=T0,
                    T_a_room=T_a_room,
                )

            # Pressure-ratio envelope event of the final operating point.
            # Floor -> the ratio is held on it and the cycle is solved;
            # ceiling -> rejected (the off state below). Nothing is printed.
            pr_event = self._last_pr_event

            # opt_success=True at the infeasible sentinel is a false success:
            # the optimiser converged but never escaped the penalty region. A
            # capacity-limited optimum sits in its own band below that sentinel
            # and counts as success — the machine ran flat out and delivered
            # less than asked, which is operation, not failure.
            opt_fun = float(getattr(opt_result, "fun", OBJ_INFEASIBLE))
            opt_success = bool(getattr(opt_result, "success", False)) and opt_fun < OBJ_INFEASIBLE
            # Why the least-lift point of this request is not an operating
            # point, when the search found none: the limit that refuses the
            # request where it is easiest to meet. The probe the search ends on
            # is an arbitrary approach pair, and the limit it happens to break
            # (the pressure ratio at 15 K + 15 K, say) need not be the one in
            # the way.
            least_lift_reason = getattr(opt_result, "least_lift_reason", None)
            if (result is None or not result.get("converged", False)) and least_lift_reason is not None:
                failure_reason = "hx_not_converged" if least_lift_reason == self._AIR_SIDE else least_lift_reason
            elif result is None:
                # Distinguish a pressure-ratio ceiling rejection from a generic
                # invalid cycle so downstream consumers see the specific cause.
                failure_reason = (
                    pr_event[0] if pr_event is not None and pr_event[0] != "pr_below_min" else "cycle_invalid"
                )
            elif not result.get("converged", False):
                failure_reason = "hx_not_converged"
            elif not opt_success:
                failure_reason = "optimizer_failed"
            else:
                failure_reason = "none"

            # A wet coil refused by the fans' smallest airflows is refused from
            # below: its answer is the smallest continuous duty, further down.
            unsolved = failure_reason not in ("none", self._MIN_AIRFLOW) and (
                result is None or not result.get("converged", False)
            )
            limited = (
                failure_reason == "none"
                and result is not None
                and result.get("capacity_clamped") == CAPACITY_CLAMPED_MAX
            )
            if unsolved or limited:
                # The request has no operating point of its own: the compressor
                # runs out of speed, or the envelope or a coil binds first. The
                # unit then runs at its ceiling (:meth:`max_capacity`), which is
                # solved rather than searched -- ranking capacity-limited
                # candidates by delivered heat walks into states that starve
                # the outdoor coil (see :meth:`max_capacity`). A capacity-limited
                # search result stands only if the ceiling cannot be solved.
                # Match the existing numerical off-state fallback if the
                # envelope search itself encounters an invalid cycle.
